_readme: Every tunable number in the loot system. The game and the loot editor BOTH read
this file, so it is the single source of truth — there are no pricing constants
hidden in code. The loot editor can override any of it live and export a
COSTS are in 'points'. The scale is fixed by two design anchors: +1 attack = 10
and +1 AC = 20. Everything else was measured against those anchors by the
valuation harness (node sim/value.mjs) — see sim/README.md for the method and
for the short list of bonuses it cannot measure.
An item's BUDGET is (intercept + perIlvl * ilvl) * slotWeight * rarityMult.
The base item is charged against that budget, and whatever is left buys affixes.
That is what makes a hand-maintained minimum-floor table unnecessary: an item a
low budget cannot afford simply cannot roll.

costs._note: Cost per 1 unit of each bonus key. Measured values from sim/value.mjs at 120 trials. NOTE: `grantSpellPerLevel` is priced but NOT YET WIRED — granted spells do not exist as an affix yet (leveled spell SLOTS do, via slot1..slot9).

elemTypeMult._note: Commonly-resisted damage types are cheaper; rarely-resisted ones cost more.

budget._note: budget = (intercept + perIlvl * ilvl) * slotWeight * rarityMult. Base items carry NO stat bonuses — only chassis (damage dice, armorBase, acBase) — so a base is gated purely by its dice/AC. perIlvl is set so armor still spreads across the career (Plate ~ilvl 11); weapons saturate early by construction, since the die range only spans ~46 points, and their progression comes from affixes instead.

slotWeight._note: Big slots carry more power than small ones, so a ring can't out-stat a greatsword.

rarityMult._note: Deliberately FLAT compared to the old 1.0/1.7/2.5/3.5/4.8 value curve. This is what stops the power spike and keeps deep commons competitive with shallow epics.

affixSlots._note: Affix LINES (not magnitudes). Rarity buys breadth, not raw power. `_perIlvl` grants one extra line every N item levels — without it the budget curve outruns affix capacity at high ilvl and deep items silently underspend. `_max` is the hard ceiling so a tooltip stays readable. `_maxPerIlvl` grants every affix +1 to its own magnitude cap every N ilvls, so deep budgets can actually be spent.

rarityWeights._note: Drop chance only — there is NO rarity gate any more. weight = clamp(base + perTier*questTier, min, max). Every rarity is rollable at every depth; the flat rarityMult is what makes an early legendary a treat rather than a run-breaker. Legendary sits near 0.07% at tier 1 rising to ~0.7% at tier 20 — lottery odds, so finding one is an event.

sourceIlvl._note: ilvl comes from the QUEST TIER plus a per-source offset — never from the floor you happen to be standing on. Depth within a dungeon leans rarity, not item level.

basePricing._note: How much of the budget the base item itself eats. damageDieRef is the free baseline die (a d4 costs nothing); every point of average damage above it costs `costs.dmg`.

gold._note: Shop/sell value derived from the item's real point cost, so pricing and economy can never drift apart.

perks._note: Perks are BUDGET-EXEMPT and exclusive to the top rarity. Their power comes from the found-ilvl band (PERK_MAGS in items.json), not from budget — otherwise a low-ilvl legendary could not afford its own defining feature. Costs below are from sim/value.mjs and are informational: they rank perks against each other, they are not spent.

unmeasured._note: The harness cannot price these — see sim/README.md. lifesteal is a censored LOWER bound; phaseStep procs on kill and nothing dies in the harness's defense mode, so its 1 is a measurement gap, not a weak perk.

startingGear._note: Tier 0: zero budget, zero bonuses, bottom-of-ladder bases. Anything found on a level-1 quest should beat it immediately.

pity._note: NOT YET WIRED — these knobs are read by nothing today. Anti-drought guarantee: random slot selection across 11 slots is the real cause of dry spells, not the curves. Intended behaviour: after `dropsWithoutUpgrade` drops that failed to beat a hero's current gear by `upgradeMargin` points, force the next roll into their weakest slot.
